spriteStudies: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: transparent VFX sprite source sheet for Biggas Hover Racing, a low-poly hover racing game with comic ink and ivory paper aesthetic. Generate a square 4 by 4 grid of exactly 16 isolated sprites on genuinely transparent background, no labels, no grid lines, no floor line, no shadows outside the sprites. Each cell is same size; all sprites fully contained with generous transparent padding, centered. Row 1: four sequential stages of a directional drift smoke puff, from tiny angular ivory wisp to expanding jagged cream cloud to fragmented fading dither. Row 2: four independent ground decal variants viewed exactly top down: short broken dark skid scuff, longer curved broken skid trace, irregular dark purple-black oil puddle with very sparse muted teal and violet glints, smaller satellite oil splatter. Row 3: four sequential bomb impact stages: small ivory yellow star, large angular orange ochre starburst with ivory core, charcoal smoke with orange embers, dissipating charcoal cloud. Row4: four independent support sprites: turquoise sharp scrape star, amber sharp sparks fan, small dark oil droplets splash, top down dark scorched star decal. Strict pixel art chunky stepped edges, clusters of flat colors, sparse ordered dithering, 3 to 4 shades per sprite. Offwhite paper #f3efdf, charcoal #262c32, muted teal #64c5b3, warm orange #ed8c37. No pure smooth white, realistic volumetrics, glow, bloom, gradients, antialiasing, text, objects or vehicles. Cohesive professionally drawn effects; smoke directional and low rather than round bubble clouds. These are source studies to validate and cut into runtime textures later.
styleComparison: Create a landscape art direction comparison board for Biggas Hover Racing. Input screenshot is a reference of the ACTUAL GAME; preserve its distinctive teal and orange hover ship rear view, ochre road, teal structures, ivory ink comic clouds and paper-halftone rendering. Show three equally sized side-by-side panels of the same closer cropped rear chase view of this hover ship drifting on this road. No UI HUD. Each panel has a modest two-line label on an ivory header. Left 'A / RETRO SECO', middle 'B / PIXEL-COMIC', right 'C / ARCADE INTENSO'. A has very sparse small ivory hard pixel smoke puffs behind lateral hover pods, tiny turquoise sparks, broken charcoal ground scuffs. B recommended direction has medium-sized angular ivory smoke plumes with muted gray two-tone shading and sparse dither, a few sharp amber and turquoise spark sprites next to hover pods, short fragmented ground skid traces following the curve. Smoke stays below ship cockpit and behind it. C has larger white smoke plumes, more bright turquoise and orange impact-like sparks and longer ground traces, deliberately more theatrical but still readable. All effects crisp pixel clusters, not volumetric or photoreal. All three treatments belong to the game's paper comic aesthetic and all have identical scale/camera/lighting for fair comparison. Simple refined presentation, footer 'MOCKUPS DE DIRECCION VISUAL'. This is an illustrated concept mockup, not a real engine screenshot. No invented gameplay UI, no cars, no tires. Keep ship silhouette clearly visible. Differences visible but tasteful.
